ne1ad032b413.s:
Consider the following about protests against the Rowlatt Act:
1. Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in opposition to the Act.
2. Jinnah, Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq drafted the Hunter Committee report.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
ne1ad032b413.x: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned in opposition to the Rowlatt legislation; they did not draft the Hunter Committee report.

n07fc8a550a8.s:
Consider the following about the Rowlatt Satyagraha:
1. It was the first all-India mass strike.
2. It was primarily urban-centred.
3. It remained confined to rural Punjab.
Which of the above statements are correct?
n07fc8a550a8.x: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first all-India mass strike and was urban-centred, though it later turned violent in Punjab and Ahmedabad; it was not confined to rural Punjab.

n7f9b8448044.s: Gandhi withdrew the Rowlatt Satyagraha on 18 April 1919 because of:
o: Acceptance of Congress demands by the Hunter Committee
Advice of the Home Rule League
n7f9b8448044.x: The movement turned violent in Punjab and Ahmedabad, so Gandhi called it a Himalayan blunder and withdrew it on 18 April 1919.

nindian-history-26-2-17.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
nindian-history-26-2-17.x: Champaran (1917) was the indigo satyagraha; Kheda (1918) was the peasant satyagraha, Ahmedabad (1918) the mill workers' strike and Dandi (1930) the Salt March.

nindian-history-122-9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the events of April 1919 in Punjab?
o: A country-wide strike took place on 6 April 1919
The Jallianwala Bagh crowd had gathered for a protest and Baisakhi
Kitchlew and Satyapal were arrested on 13 April 1919
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919
nindian-history-122-9.x: Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal were arrested on 9 April 1919, not 13 April; 13 April was the day of the massacre.

nindian-history-122-15.s: How did Rabindranath Tagore protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
o: Resigned from the Viceroy's Executive Council
Resigned from the Imperial Legislative Council
nindian-history-122-15.x: Tagore gave up his knighthood on 31 May 1919 in protest; it was Shankaran Nair who resigned from the Viceroy's Council.

n759c568bfbc.s: The Khilafat leaders opposed which treaty imposed on the Ottoman Empire after the First World War?
n759c568bfbc.x: The Treaty of Sevres (May 1920) threatened the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire and intensified the Khilafat agitation.

n422a604690a.s: The Khilafat agitation lost its relevance when Turkey abolished the Caliphate in:
n422a604690a.x: Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924, removing the central issue around which the Khilafat agitation had developed.

n988aea7e355.s:
Consider the following about the Non-Cooperation Movement:
1. It achieved Swaraj within one year.
2. It made the Indian National Congress a mass force for the first time.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n988aea7e355.x: Swaraj was not achieved within one year, but the NCM became the first nationwide mass movement and made the Congress a mass force.

n67d725fd175.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Moplah uprising
B. Prince of Wales boycott
C. Chauri Chaura incident
D. Formation of the Swaraj Party
n67d725fd175.x: Moplah uprising (August 1921), Prince of Wales boycott (17 November 1921), Chauri Chaura (February 1922), Swaraj Party (1923).

ndfaede16a24.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Formation of the Swaraj Party
2. Prince of Wales boycott
3. Gandhi's arrest
4. Bardoli resolution
ndfaede16a24.x: Prince of Wales boycott (17 November 1921), Bardoli resolution (11–12 February 1922), Gandhi's arrest (March 1922), Swaraj Party (1923).

n71ea7e74320.s:
Consider the following about Gandhi's approach to the Khilafat issue:
1. He merged the Khilafat cause with the Swaraj cause.
2. He saw it as an opportunity to forge Hindu-Muslim unity.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n71ea7e74320.x: Gandhi merged the Khilafat cause with Swaraj and regarded it as an opportunity to forge Hindu-Muslim unity.

n5496f08b529.s: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase is regarded as the high point of:
n5496f08b529.x: The Khilafat–Non-Cooperation phase represented the high point of Hindu-Muslim unity during the national movement.

nap-history-25-8.s: The Home Rule League, whose Andhra branches were started under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, was founded by:
nap-history-25-8.x: Annie Besant founded the Home Rule Movement in 1916; its Andhra branches were started under Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.

ne9584cc2671.s: Which of the following pairs of movement and leader is correctly matched?
ne9584cc2671.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the Palnadu forest satyagraha; Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya led Chirala-Perala and Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary led Pedanandipadu.

nap-history-25-26.s:
Consider the following about the Wahabi Movement:
1. It was pro-British.
2. In Hyderabad, it was led by Mubariz-ud-Daulah.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nap-history-25-26.x: The Wahabi Movement was anti-British, not pro-British; in Hyderabad it was led by Mubariz-ud-Daulah.

n3c53000c051.s: Which of the following pairs of work and author is correctly matched?
n3c53000c051.x: Viplava Parivarthanam was by Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri; Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu was by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary and Makoddi Telladoratanam by Garimella Satyanarayana.

nf6d10c44529.s: After the Congress boycotted the November 1920 elections in Madras Presidency, the first ministry was formed by:
nf6d10c44529.x: The Justice Party won 63 of 98 seats and the first ministry was formed under A. Subbarayalu Reddiar on 17 December 1920.

nbd8962aec83.s: After the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement, the pro-changers favoured:
nbd8962aec83.x: The pro-changers, or Swarajists, sought to enter the councils to 'end or mend' them; the no-changers preferred constructive work and continued boycott.

n2e021fea522.s:
Consider the following about the Palnadu forest satyagraha:
1. Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari studied and supported it.
2. Konda Venkatappayya tried to moderate it, as the Congress favoured social boycott rather than tax refusal.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n2e021fea522.x: Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Madabhushi Vedantam Narasimhachari backed the movement, while Konda Venkatappayya tried to moderate it because the Congress favoured social boycott over tax refusal.

na2bbf055afe.s: Which of the following pairs of leader and title is correctly matched?
na2bbf055afe.x: Konda Venkatappaiah was known as Desabhakta; Duggirala was Andhra Ratna, Prakasam was Andhra Kesari and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was Desoddharaka.

nd2bf7d55691.s:
Consider the following:
1. The Swarajists favoured entry into the councils.
2. The No-Changers favoured council entry over constructive work.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nd2bf7d55691.x: The Swarajists favoured council entry, while the No-Changers concentrated on constructive work and continued the boycott; both reunited at Belgaum in 1924.

n79475fb0a56.s:
Consider the following about the Dandi March:
1. Gandhi began it from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 with 78 followers.
2. The route covered about 240 kilometres.
3. He broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.
Which of the above statements are correct?
n79475fb0a56.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is wrong because the route was about 240 miles (385 km), not 240 km.

nf9337052d2b.s:
Consider the following about women in the Civil Disobedience Movement:
1. Women joined in massive numbers, including picketing liquor and foreign-cloth shops.
2. Women participated only after the movement was withdrawn in 1934.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
nf9337052d2b.x: The CDM was the first occasion on which women participated in massive numbers, picketing liquor shops and foreign-cloth shops.

n2517fb75470.s:
Consider the following about the Civil Disobedience Movement:
1. It was confined exclusively to urban merchants and lawyers.
2. It was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n2517fb75470.x: The CDM was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale, drawing women, peasants, tribals and merchants into the struggle.

nindian-history-100-6.s:
Consider the following:
1. The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920.
2. The Quit India Movement began in 1931.
3. The Civil Disobedience Movement began in 1930.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-history-100-6.x: Non-Cooperation began in 1920 and Civil Disobedience in 1930; statement 2 is false because Quit India began in 1942.

nindian-history-23-13.s: Which tax was the main target of the Civil Disobedience Movement launched in 1930?
nindian-history-23-13.x: The salt tax was the main target of the Civil Disobedience Movement, launched with Gandhi's Dandi March in 1930.

n7527977b744.s: Which of the following Salt Satyagraha centres in Andhra is correctly matched with its leader?
n7527977b744.x: Bulusu Sambamurthy led at Chollangi near Kakinada; Kasi Viswanadham led at Vadarevu, Bezawada Gopal Reddy at Mylapadu and Kalluri Subbarao at Bellary.

n5c7e4b6432c.s: Which was the first Salt Satyagraha centre in Andhra, beginning on 6 April 1930?
n5c7e4b6432c.x: Machilipatnam was the first Andhra Salt Satyagraha centre, beginning on 6 April 1930.

na5b23d0a555.s:
Consider the following about Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi:
1. She was the first woman graduate in Andhra and the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha.
2. She led twenty women to make salt at the High Court beach in Madras.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
na5b23d0a555.x: Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi was the first woman graduate in Andhra and the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha; the High Court beach march of twenty women was led by Durgabai Deshmukh.

n8583b3da392.s:
Consider the following about the Karachi session of the Congress (March 1931):
1. It was presided over by Vallabhbhai Patel.
2. Its resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme was drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru.
3. It rejected the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
Which of the above statements are correct?
n8583b3da392.x: Patel presided and Nehru drafted the Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme resolution; statement 3 is wrong because Karachi endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

n599cbd58158.s: The Karachi resolution of 1931 foreshadowed which parts of the Constitution of India?
n599cbd58158.x: The Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme foreshadowed Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy).

nindian-history-130-13.s: Which of the following pairs about the Cripps Mission is correctly matched?
o: Head of the Mission – Winston Churchill
Congress President during the talks – Jawaharlal Nehru
British Prime Minister who sent it – Clement Attlee
nindian-history-130-13.x: The Cripps Mission arrived in March 1942; it was headed by Sir Stafford Cripps, sent by Winston Churchill, and Maulana Azad was Congress President during the talks.

n60554cb680b.s:
Consider the following about the responses to the August Offer (1940):
1. The Congress rejected it.
2. The Muslim League welcomed its minority veto.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n60554cb680b.x: The Congress rejected the August Offer (Nehru called dominion status 'dead as a doornail'); the Muslim League welcomed the minority veto but held that only partition would satisfy it.

n696003cd4e5.s:
Consider the following:
1. The August Offer first accepted a post-war constitution-making body.
2. The August Offer first conceded the provincial option to opt out of the Indian Union.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n696003cd4e5.x: The August Offer first accepted a post-war constitution-making body; it was the Cripps Mission that first conceded the provincial opt-out, the germ of Partition.

nfb1286b35d2.s: The Quit India Movement of 1942 was Gandhi's:
o: Movement that won immediate transfer of power
nfb1286b35d2.x: The Quit India Movement was Gandhi's final mass movement and showed that Indian independence could not be postponed after the war.

nindian-history-113-14.s: Which of the following pairs of slogan and leader is correctly matched?
o: “Give me blood… freedom” – Subhas Chandra Bose
nindian-history-113-14.x: “Give me blood… freedom” was Bose's; “Swaraj is my birthright” was Tilak's, “Do or Die” Gandhi's and “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” Shastri's.

nindian-history-113-6.s: Which of the following pairs of leader and slogan is wrongly matched?
o: Subhas Chandra Bose – “Give me blood… freedom”
nindian-history-113-6.x: “Back to the Vedas” was Dayanand Saraswati's call, not C.R. Das's; the other three pairs are correct.

nindian-history-112-3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Tilak said, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it.”
Gandhi's words “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight” belong to the Quit India Movement
Gandhi gave the call “Do or Die” in August 1942
Tagore said, “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight.”
nindian-history-112-3.x: “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight” was said by Gandhi during Quit India, not by Tagore.

nf0724fd833d.s: What was the CPI's stand on the Quit India Movement after its ban was lifted on 23 July 1942?
o: It led the underground movement in Andhra
It backed the British war effort and opposed Quit India
It ran the secret Congress Radio
It stayed neutral and boycotted the 1945 elections
nf0724fd833d.x: After its ban was lifted the CPI backed the British war effort and opposed Quit India; the underground and secret radio were led by Congress Socialists.

n898e9559dcf.s: Which leaders were associated with the Andhra branch of the Forward Bloc?
o: Kala Venkata Rao and Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah
n898e9559dcf.x: Madduri Annapurnaiah and Peta Bapayya were associated with the Andhra branch of the Forward Bloc.

nindian-history-101-3.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the INA is correctly matched?
o: Rash Behari Bose – Japanese officer who headed the F-Kikan
Major Iwaichi Fujiwara – Handed INA command to Subhas Chandra Bose
Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon – First operational commander
Captain Mohan Singh – First operational commander
nindian-history-101-3.x: Captain Mohan Singh was the first INA commander; Fujiwara headed the F-Kikan, Giani Pritam Singh helped conceive the INA and Rash Behari Bose handed command to Subhas Bose.

n9c3534f1e88.s:
Consider the following about the INA trials and the RIN Mutiny:
1. They strengthened the loyalty of the Indian armed forces to the Raj.
2. They showed that the British could no longer rely on the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n9c3534f1e88.x: The INA trials and the RIN Mutiny showed that the British could no longer rely confidently on the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.

nindian-history-101-18.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the INA Trials is correctly matched?
o: Shah Nawaz Khan – Leading defence counsel
Bhulabhai Desai – Officer who married Captain Lakshmi
Prem Kumar Sehgal – Later became a Union minister
Red Fort, Delhi – Venue of the trials
nindian-history-101-18.x: The INA Trials were held at the Red Fort; Bhulabhai Desai led the defence, Shah Nawaz Khan later became a Union minister and Prem Kumar Sehgal married Captain Lakshmi.

n428b1568557.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Father of the Nation – Subhas Chandra Bose
Netaji – Subhas Chandra Bose, a title given by the people of Germany
Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani – Indian National Congress
n428b1568557.x: The title 'Netaji' was given to Bose by the people of Germany; Gandhi called Bose the 'Patriot of patriots', and Bose called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'.

ne79c55d8beb.s: The call 'Do or Die' was given in 1942 by:
ne79c55d8beb.x: 'Do or Die' was Gandhi's call at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942; Meherally coined 'Quit India' and Bose's war cry was 'Dilli Chalo'.

nindian-history-100-45.s: The Quit India Resolution was passed at Bombay on:
nindian-history-100-45.x: The Quit India Resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942; the Wardha CWC met on 14 July and the leaders were arrested on 9 August.

nbcfa416b57c.s:
Consider the following about the inquiries into the death of Subhas Chandra Bose:
1. The Shah Nawaz Committee concluded that he died in the crash.
2. The Khosla Commission concluded that he died in the crash.
3. The government accepted the Mukherjee Commission report in 2006.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nbcfa416b57c.x: The Shah Nawaz Committee and the Khosla Commission accepted the crash; the Mukherjee Commission said he did not die in it, but the government rejected its report in 2006.

ne4b58eb8423.s: The INA Defence Committee was set up by:
ne4b58eb8423.x: The INA Defence Committee was established by the Congress to defend the accused INA officers.

n937265e4fa2.s:
Consider the following about the RIN revolt of 1946:
1. Sections of the RIAF and the Army also showed disaffection.
2. The revolt was confined to civilian workers.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n937265e4fa2.x: Sections of the Royal Indian Air Force and the Army also showed disaffection during the RIN revolt, which was a revolt of naval ratings, not civilian workers.

n73c042e1fff.s: The INA trials and the RIN revolt alarmed the British mainly because they showed that:
o: The Cabinet Mission had already failed
The Indian Army could no longer be fully trusted
The princely states had turned against Britain
The Muslim League had merged with the Congress
n73c042e1fff.x: The British depended on the 2.5-million-strong Indian Army; the INA trials and RIN revolt showed its loyalty could no longer be assumed.

nindian-history-114-5.s:
Consider the following:
1. The Indian National Liberal Federation was founded in 1918.
2. The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923.
3. The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-history-114-5.x: All three are correct: the Moderates formed the Liberal Federation in 1918, the Swaraj Party came in 1923 and the Congress Socialist Party in 1934.

nindian-history-114-7.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Home Rule League – Tilak and Annie Besant
Ghadar Party – Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
nindian-history-114-7.x: Abhinav Bharat was founded by V.D. Savarkar, not Subhas Chandra Bose; the other three pairs are correct.

nindian-history-114-18.s: Which of the following pairs of party and founder is correctly matched?
o: Socialist Party – C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru
nindian-history-114-18.x: Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party; the Swaraj Party was founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, the Socialist Party by JP and the Forward Bloc by Bose.

nf78cdda60ec.s: Which of the following satyagrahas was led by Vallabhbhai Patel rather than Gandhi?
nf78cdda60ec.x: The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by Patel; Champaran, the Ahmedabad Mill Strike and the Dandi March were led by Gandhi.

nindian-history-104-1.s: Who was the temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly when it first met on 9 December 1946?
nindian-history-104-1.x: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was temporary Chairman; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.

n632a7e8715a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Statue of Unity?
o: It was sculpted by Ram V. Sutar
n632a7e8715a.x: The Statue of Unity is in Gujarat (facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam), not Hyderabad.

n1cc5980bc5b.s:
Consider the following about the Sardar Patel National Unity Award:
1. It was instituted in 2019.
2. It is given exclusively to members of the armed forces.
3. It carries no cash component and not more than three awards are given in a year.
Which of the above statements are correct?
n1cc5980bc5b.x: Instituted in 2019 for contributions to unity and integrity, the award carries a medal and citation but no cash, with at most three recipients a year; it is not limited to the armed forces.

naa199c50c00.s: Besides Vallabhbhai Patel, who is said to be the only other person in India to receive the title 'Sardar'?
naa199c50c00.x: Gouthu Latchanna of Srikakulam is said to be the only other person in India to receive the title 'Sardar'.

ndc7ddffe721.s: Which of the following pairs of leader and region is correctly matched?
ndc7ddffe721.x: Sewa Singh Thikriwala was associated with Punjab; Pathik with Rajasthan, Sarangadhar Das with Orissa and Ramananda Tirtha with the Hyderabad State Congress.

n18b96289280.s:
Consider the following about Junagadh in 1947–48:
1. The Nawab acceded to Pakistan in September 1947.
2. The Nawab fled after an economic blockade.
3. The plebiscite of February 1948 favoured Pakistan.
Which of the above statements are correct?
n18b96289280.x: The Nawab acceded to Pakistan and fled after an economic blockade, but the February 1948 plebiscite went in favour of India.

n3ba585a2a07.s:
Consider the following:
1. Dewan C.P. Ramaswami Iyer declared the independence of Travancore.
2. Jinnah tried to win over the Maharaja of Jodhpur.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n3ba585a2a07.x: Dewan C.P. Ramaswami Iyer declared Travancore's independence, and Maharaja Hanwant Singh of Jodhpur was tempted by Jinnah.

na8d418aeebd.s: Which of the following pairs of operation and commander is correctly matched?
o: Operation Polo – Maj. Gen. K.P. Candeth
Operation Vijay – Maj. Gen. El Edroos
Operation Polo – Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri
Operation Vijay – Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri
na8d418aeebd.x: Operation Polo (Hyderabad, 1948) was led by Maj. Gen. J.N. Chaudhuri; Operation Vijay (Goa, 1961) was led by K.P. Candeth, and El Edroos was the Nizam's army chief.

n37e62fc8a29.s: Yanam, a French-origin enclave inside Andhra Pradesh, is administered as part of:
n37e62fc8a29.x: Yanam lies inside Andhra Pradesh's Godavari delta but is administered as part of the Puducherry Union Territory.

n097983af4d0.s: Which event immediately preceded the formation of the Interim Government on 2 September 1946?
o: Direct Action Day of the Muslim League
The Assembly sitting as Dominion Legislature
n097983af4d0.x: The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946, shortly before the Interim Government was formed on 2 September 1946.

nindian-history-117-7.s:
Consider the following:
1. The first Jesuit Mission is associated with the year 1580.
2. The Serampore Mission is associated with the year 1800.
3. The Cripps Mission is associated with the year 1945.
Which of the above statements are correct?
nindian-history-117-7.x: The first Jesuit mission reached Akbar in 1580 and the Serampore Mission began in 1800; the Cripps Mission came in 1942, not 1945.

n3cf97763e40.s: The core proposal of the August Offer of 1940 was:
o: An Indian-framed constitution after the war
A weak Union through provincial grouping
n3cf97763e40.x: The August Offer accepted the demand for an Indian-framed constitution after the war; the other proposals belong to later schemes.

n8e259449222.s: Which of the following pairs of Cabinet Mission member and British office is correctly matched?
o: Lord Pethick-Lawrence – First Lord of the Admiralty
Sir Stafford Cripps – President of the Board of Trade
A.V. Alexander – Secretary of State for India
Sir Stafford Cripps – Secretary of State for India
n8e259449222.x: Cripps was President of the Board of Trade; Pethick-Lawrence was Secretary of State for India and Alexander was First Lord of the Admiralty.

n7cdca3235d5.s:
Consider the following about provincial ministries after the 1945–46 elections:
1. The Muslim League formed the ministry in Bengal under H.S. Suhrawardy.
2. The Congress formed ministries in most provinces, including NWFP.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n7cdca3235d5.x: The League formed ministries in Bengal under Suhrawardy and in Sindh, while the Congress formed ministries in most provinces, including NWFP.

nindian-history-105-16.s: Which of the following pairs of Interim Government member and portfolio is correctly matched?
o: Sardar Patel – Home, Information and Broadcasting, and States
nindian-history-105-16.x: Patel held Home, I&B and States; Nehru held External Affairs, Rajendra Prasad Food and Agriculture, and Baldev Singh Defence.

nindian-history-105-33.s: Liaquat Ali Khan's 1947 budget in the Interim Government was popularly called a:
nindian-history-105-33.x: Liaquat Ali Khan's 1947 budget was called a poor man's budget; its high taxes and duties hit traders and businessmen.

n6233e0f0a56.s:
Consider the following about Gandhi's peace mission in Noakhali (1946–47):
1. He walked from village to village for peace but failed to stop the violence.
2. It was undertaken before Direct Action Day.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
n6233e0f0a56.x: Gandhi walked village to village in Noakhali but failed to stop the violence; the mission came after Direct Action Day (16 August 1946), whose riots spread to Noakhali.

nindian-history-105-20.s: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Interim Government formed in 1946?
nindian-history-105-20.x: Liaquat Ali Khan (Finance), Baldev Singh (Defence) and Asaf Ali (Railways and Transport) were members of the Interim Government; B.R. Ambedkar was not.
